title: Salt Lake County Homes and Nonprofits Get Makeovers During Zions Bank’s 34th Annual Paint-a-Thon
summary: 1,231 Zions employees volunteered at both homes and non-profit organizations.
body_markdown:
SALT LAKE CITY, Utah; June 4, 2026 – Nine homes and Nine nonprofits in Salt Lake City got makeovers this week as a part of Zions Bank’ annual Paint-a-Thon service project. Dozens of Zions bankers rolled up their sleeves and rolled paint on the walls for homes and non-profit organizations across Utah and Idaho as a part of Paint-a-Thon.


Salt Lake County had a wide range of projects with schools, homes, mobile homes and nonprofit organizations, including the nonprofits Women of World and Housing Connect.


In this 34th year of Paint-a-Thon, 1,231 Zions employees volunteered at both homes and non-profit organizations. In total, nine homes, nine non-profits and four schools received a fresh coat of paint and a refresh of their landscaping, directly or indirectly benefitting thousands of Utahns. An additional seven projects were also completed in Idaho.


“I’m very excited to be participating in Paint-a-Thon this year for the first time,” said Zions Bank President and CEO Nathan Callister. “This is a great opportunity for us to give back to the community. It’s a great cause.”


“The crew is nice. Everyone is excited. Everyone is happy. This is nice environment.” said homeowner Amid Amidbakarr on the first night of Paint-a-Thon, “I want to say thank you very much to Zions Bank. I will not miss the old paint when it is gone.”


Paint-a-Thon aims to help older or low-income adults, as well as people with disabilities and veteran homeowners take pride in their homes and maintain their independence. With the addition of non-profit facilities, the Paint-a-Thon project also hopes to brighten communities and raise awareness for the non-profit partners’ missions.


Projects completed during the annual week-long event were selected with the assistance of nominations from the public, state housing agencies, community organizations and local churches.


Launched in 1991, Zions Bank’s Paint-a-Thon began as a volunteer project for a dozen homes along Utah’s Wasatch Front. Over the three decades, Zions Bank employees have set aside summer pastimes for a week each year — volunteering in the evenings after work — to paint 1,331 homes and non-profits throughout Idaho, Utah and Wyoming. Not counting the dollar value of volunteer hours through the years, the bank has donated more than $1.5 million toward beautifying communities in the three states.


**About Zions Bank**


Zions Bank is Utah’s oldest financial institution and is the only local bank with a statewide distribution of branches operating 95 full-service branches. Zions Bank also operates 26 branches in Idaho and Wyoming. In addition to offering a wide range of traditional banking services, Zions Bank is also a leader in small business lending. Founded in 1873, Zions Bank has been serving the communities of Utah for more than 150 years. Additional information is available at zionsbank.com. Zions Bank is a division of Zions Bancorporation N.A., Member FDIC.
